**Finding: compliant (no redline).**

The Agreement contains no audit, inspection or verification right running against Sparkling. I checked the planner's candidate sections (§3 Restrictions on Use, §20 General Matters and its continuation, §10 Maintenance, §14 Confidentiality) plus §11 Fees, and ran targeted searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "records", "premises", "monitor", "comply" and "access". The only hits are Sparkling's own telephone support access (p0073) and the mutual confidentiality definition (p0095) — neither creates a verification right, and there is no remote or direct system-access language.

Since the risk this rule guards against (frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access) simply does not exist here, the document sits better than the preferred position. Consistent with the direction principle, we do not propose inserting an audit right against our own party.
